headline: A Spot team member wrote on Spot's GitHub forum that an observability system was breached via a compromised credential; still Reported.
summary: New source s004 (Tier 4): Rackspace Spot's GitHub Discussions thread 'Update On Spot Outage', Nov 20, where a Spot team member said an observability system was breached using a compromised credential and that intrusive infrastructure changes caused the extended outage, then gave a 9am Pacific Nov 21 restoration estimate. Added c012 (Reported), t005 and t006; added s004 to c003, c004 and c011. c001 stays Reported: a forum post is Tier 4 and not a Rackspace-hosted statement. c011 stays Not established: no published incident report, and whose credential and how it leaked are unknown. Rackspace release notes and status page unchanged (sign-up restriction notice still pinned, no breach mention). Other new coverage (Mezha, infonewscyber.fr) rewrites BleepingComputer, same independence group; no second independent outlet. BleepingComputer read through a search tool. Reddit not checked: access blocked. Staleness check done: q001 answer and incident.json known/not_known refreshed. Privacy check done: no names, usernames or handles.
author: Research agent

headline: Rackspace reportedly told customers leaked credentials let someone into Spot on Nov 17; not confirmed on a Rackspace page.
summary: First draft. 3 sources (2 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2), 11 claims (2 Confirmed, 5 Reported, 4 Not established), 5 questions. BleepingComputer, Nov 21, quotes Rackspace's customer notice: unauthorized access with leaked credentials, pods created, Kubernetes Secrets readable, admin console down for days, service restored Nov 21. Rackspace's own release notes and status page (Tier 1) do not mention a breach, so the hack stays Reported. Data theft, number of customers, attacker and how the credentials leaked are Not established. BleepingComputer was read through a fetch tool because the site blocks direct automated reading. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.
